summary: Specializing in archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, J. P. Mallory studied at Occidental College (~1963–1967) and UCLA (~1970–1975). He held posts at Queen's University Belfast (~1977–2010) and Queen's University at Kingston (attested 2014).

An Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University (-1872) under Hendrik Kern, J. S. Speyer lectured at the University of Amsterdam (1877), was professor of Latin at the University of Groningen (1888–1903), and professor of Sanskrit at Leiden.

J. Thomas Rimer, a scholar of Japanese studies, was educated at Princeton University and Columbia University. He held positions at UCLA (~1965–1971), Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1983), the University of Maryland (~1985–1988), and the University of Pittsburgh (~1988–2010).
Jaan Puhvel studied under Georges Dumézil (~1952–1953) and Stig Wikander (~1953–1954), and later taught C. Scott Littleton.
Working in Indology and religious studies, Jack C. Laughlin earned his PhD at McMaster University (-1999) and held a post at the University of Sudbury.
Jack Goody, who worked in history and archaeology, studied at St Albans School and St John's College (~1938–1946). He spent his academic career at the University of Cambridge (~1954–1984).

A scholar and teacher of Buddhist and religious studies, Jack Kornfield studied at Dartmouth College, Saybrook University (PhD), and under Wing-tsit Chan, Ajahn Chah, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Dipa Ma. He co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Spirit Rock Meditation Center.

Jacob Ensink worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (~1945–1952). He joined the University of Groningen in 1954 as a lecturer and later became professor.

Active in linguistics and history, Jacob Grimm studied at the University of Marburg (~1802–1806). He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and the Frederick William University Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).

Jacob N. Kinnard works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He has held academic posts as Assistant Professor of Religion at the College of William & Mary and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Religious studies scholar Jacob Neusner studied at Harvard, Lincoln College, Columbia, and the Jewish Theological Seminary. He held posts at UW–Milwaukee (~1961–1962), Brandeis (~1962–1964), the University of South Florida (~1990–2000), and Bard College (~1994–2014).

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jacob P. Dalton completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (-2002) under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held posts at SOAS, Yale University (2005), and the University of California, Berkeley.

Linguist and Indologist Jacob Wackernagel studied at Basel, Göttingen, Leipzig, and Oxford, learning from Friedrich Nietzsche and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the University of Basel (1876–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).

Jacqueline I. Stone, a scholar of Buddhist and Japanese studies, earned degrees at San Francisco State University and UCLA, studying under William R. LaFleur. She served as Professor at Princeton University (1990–2019) and holds an affiliation with Minobusan University.

Working in Indology and religious studies, Jacqueline Suthren Hirst completed her doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. She has held posts at the University of Manchester, including as Honorary Research Fellow.

Jacques André was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (-1948). He held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1919–1938), the University of Paris (~1936–1958), and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1945–1954).

Jacques Gernet, a scholar of sinology and history, studied at Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at EPHE/EHESS (1955–1976), the University of Paris (1957–1968), Paris Diderot University (~1968–1973), and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied at Beaux-Arts de Paris and Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and served as curator and president (2008–2011) at the Musée Guimet.
